Research Report · refreshed 2026-10-22 · For James Boggs, IDE profile owner

The Softmax IDE Today: Surfaces, Primitives, System Map and Profiles

Research report for James Boggs (owner of the IDE's Hermes profile distributions), refreshed 2026-10-22 PDT. The code citations refer to metta c5de75f1d3 and ide-distributions ed1ded5, unless a passage gives a different commit. The live IDE runs cd3626ccbf, which is a descendant of c5de75f1d3. Mason's repo did not change and stays at cad8505. The live tests occurred on 2026-10-21, 11:27–12:00 PDT, before the 10-22 coordination redesign (§7). We read Slack through 10-22 12:30 PDT. The Cogent IDE (/ide) and Play are out of scope. They appear only where they touch the hosted workspace of the IDE.

Executive summary

Two surfaces are important now, and both are live. Softmax IDE (/ide-next) is the chat-first app of Rohit and Aaron. /ide-final is Rohit's port of Mason's workspace. It is a page for the GoTA game, and the user and the orchestrator edit its layout and notes together. Both surfaces are the same Next.js package, deployed two times. Both surfaces drive one hosted workspace for each user. This workspace is a container that runs this repo's orchestrator and two researcher profiles behind metta's bridge. Rohit has a draft stack (#28801–#28805), and its purpose is to mount Mason's whole application at /ide-final. /ide-mvp is retired.

The UI and the profiles still connect in only a few places. The orchestrator answers chat and makes native Kanban tasks, and the Work board shows these tasks. Almost all other parts do not connect:

  • Each hosted turn still tells the orchestrator to use "coach tools" and IDE tools, but these tools do not exist anywhere now. The IDE's own tool server was deleted on 10-21. In live tests, this sent the orchestrator into tool searches that found nothing, and the "Improve my policy" chip failed completely.
  • The IDE features that use those tools (Research journey, goals, continuations, the tool-call ledger) stay empty against the hosted agent.
  • The orchestrator sends its background news (ide_say) to a chat log, but neither IDE surface reads that log.
  • Research records, the champion, the research pause, permit asks and the new episode budget have no UI.
  • One production bug stays in the profiles. The permit read of the shared client returns 404. As a result, promotions that wait for a permit never complete.

On 10-22, Rohit rebuilt research coordination (ide-distributions #30 with metta #28679). Now each orchestrator input (chat, task notifications, cron wakes) waits in one durable first-in, first-out queue. The orchestrator now uploads and integrates builds, and the researchers only stage them. The coach commands, card kinds and acknowledgement tools are gone. The orchestrator also selects its game and league from the conversation (#25), and it has 29 tools. Three operational facts still control each profile change. First, a merge to main here gets to new workspaces in a few minutes. Second, the orchestrator's cron job keeps each workspace awake. Third, an image update can now leave a workspace stopped until an operator does an action. §6.6 sorts the fixes, and §8 gives a critique of Rohit's /ide-final delivery plan.

1. Orientation: who builds what

  • Two IDE surfaces are live: /ide-next and /ide-final. Both surfaces are metta/packages/softmax-ide.
  • Mason's prototype client moves into /ide-final one part at a time. Aaron's Discovery and Goal loop tabs (#28101) are stranded, because they target /ide-mvp, and /ide-mvp was retired on 10-21.
  • Each hosted agent that the IDE talks to is a Hermes profile from this repo. These profiles operate on Rohit's EC2 fleet.
  • The bridge that connects the UI to those profiles is metta code, and almost all of this code is Rohit's.

On 10-19, Rohit gave the division of work in the team: "Mason / Aaron on features and ergonomics, James on semantic representations and policy improvement, me on agent infra" (Slack IDE group DM). On 10-21, Aaron asked for a game-agnostic orchestrator, because Aaron prepares a Pudge Wars IDE. Rohit agreed to "make the infrastructure and profile distribution flexible enough for any game in theory, but focus on one game (pudge wars or gota) in practice" (Slack, 10-21 18:05). Also on 10-21, James asked for a discussion "to solidify the initial primitives we want to be using" (Slack, 10-21 18:26).

Out of scope, but these surfaces share infrastructure:

  • The Cogent IDE (/ide) still drives the same IDE workspace. It is the only page that shows the orchestrator's ide_say news (§4.2). No page links to it, and no PR removes it.
  • Play now runs a second, separate workspace on the same cogent of the user (metta #28599, #28619). As a result, Play does not conflict with the IDE now.

The system in one paragraph. Each signed-in user has one hosted IDE workspace. This workspace is a sandboxed container on a shared server, and it starts on demand. In the workspace, one Hermes process serves more than one profile, and each profile is a named agent with its own prompt (SOUL.md), tools, skills and memory. For the IDE, these profiles are this repo's orchestrator and two researchers. The orchestrator (Rohit's code now calls it the "coordinator") answers the user, and the two researchers do native Hermes Kanban tasks in the background. A small bridge process in the same container moves messages between the platform API (Observatory) and the profiles. The UIs never connect to the container, but read and write records through Observatory, and the bridge relays these records. Appendix A gives the definitions of these terms.

2. What users see

  • /ide-next is chat first. The landing page has a composer and league stats. When you send a message, a two-pane workspace opens. Conversations are on the left, and tabs are on the right (Work board, Research journey, Experiments, views).
  • /ide-final is one GoTA page. It has an editable layout, a draft card for project notes, and the same chat.
  • Mason's full client has policy workspaces and an agent character. Work on this client is still in flight.

2.1 Softmax IDE (/ide-next)

  • The landing page gives a composer, four starter chips, recent chats, and league performance.
  • A chat opens the request workspace. The conversation rail is on the left, and the result tabs are on the right.

The top bar contains a History drawer ("Workspace history — Reopen a previous request in this league"), Back and Forward, a game and league picker, a daily credit pill, workspace Pause and Resume (metta #28471), and the account menu.

The composer ("Ask, learn, or give the agent a direction…") has these controls:

  • A model picker. Haiku 5.5 is the default. Since metta #28612 (10-21), the hosted path obeys this picker for chat turns1. But background turns and researchers still use the fleet's model (§5.2).
  • Chat options: Tool permissions (Ask or Auto, default Auto) and Thinking effort2.

Four chips are below the composer: Learn this game, Review the league, Develop a strategy and Improve my policy. Each chip sets a hidden mode (learn, view, do or research). This mode changes the instructions that go with the message3,4. Below the chips are "Recent chats" and the league views, Performance and Rounds. These views show rank, MMR (matchmaking rating), rounds played and a leaderboard5.

The request workspace (components/workspace/request-workspace.tsx) has two panes.

The left rail is the conversation. It contains:

  • A Main chat and a maximum of 12 child chats. All of these chats share one canvas6.
  • Tool-activity rows in the transcript. These rows come from the Hermes agent session (§3.1).
  • Task notices. Since 10-22, these notices show the native status directly, for example "Worker finished"7.
  • Approval cards with Approve and Deny (hermes-approvals.tsx).
  • An Agent workflow panel. This panel shows a list of delegated tasks, with Cancel and "Continue this chat when research finishes"8.
  • Account research controls: Pause all, Check account status, Resume and Repair.

The right canvas holds tabs:

  • Work board: Queued, Working, Needs attention and Finished, and also "Chat with researcher"9. Most chats show this tab by default.
  • Research journey: findings and checkpoints.
  • Experiments: this tab appears when a hosted evaluation receipt ("XP", an Experience Request run) arrives.
  • Game guide, App (a micro-app that the agent edits), Replay, and the Views that the agent makes.

2.2 /ide-final

  • The page is one GoTA workspace page. It has three modes: View, Arrange (drag, resize, remove) and Code (edit the layout as JSON).
  • A draft card holds a title and project notes. The page refreshes this card every 10 seconds, but it does not overwrite unsaved edits (metta #28623).
  • The page uses the chat component and composer of /ide-next again. Thus, every hosted-turn problem in §6 also applies to it.

The page also has the conversations list, Standings, the standard chat composer, and workspace Pause and Resume (components/final/workspace.tsx, metta #28649). You can customize only the workspace page.

Two documents per owner and league are behind the page: layout and draft. Each document has a revision counter (database/migrations/20261021100000_workspace_documents.sql). An ide.operation_receipts table also makes agent saves safe to retry. One SDK serves two doors.

The browser calls /api/workspace-sdk with its sign-in session11. The orchestrator calls softmax.com/ide/mcp with its player credential. The website forwards that path to the internal /ide-final/mcp of the IDE12. Both doors use the same executeWorkspaceOperation (lib/ide/sdk.ts).

There are eight operations: components.search, components.describe, layout.read, layout.validate, layout.save, draft.read, draft.save and league.overview (lib/ide/schema.ts). The league is always GoTA13.

The owner comes from the credential, never from tool arguments. The browser door keys rows by the sign-in subjectId. The MCP door keys rows by owner_user_id from Observatory /whoami, and it keeps this value in a cache for 30 seconds14. For one person, these two values are the same User ID. But the system test of the PR proved this only with fixture identities.

2.3 In flight: Mason's application and Aaron's tabs

  • Rohit's draft stack (metta #28801 to #28805) is not merged. If it merges, it will mount Mason's whole application at /ide-final: the shell, policy workspaces, agent views, custom tabs and a hosted Minion Rush tutorial. PR #28801 adds durable IDE source, publication identities, native research context and measured-goal operations.
  • Aaron's PR #28101 brings ideas from Mason's Discovery and Goal loop to /ide-mvp. But that target no longer exists.

Mason's client ("Softmax Client") is a local React app. It operates on the web and in Electron. It has these parts:

  • Sidebar: Dashboard, Players, Policies, Coworlds, Leaderboards, Cogents and Opponents15.
  • Policy workspace tabs: Info, Code, Discovery, Goal loop, R/L loop, Leaderboard, Opponents, and Custom. The agent makes the Custom tab as sandboxed HTML16.
  • Agent-rebuilt pages: the agent can rebuild any page as a JSON view of first-party components. Then the user can change the arrangement in Edit mode. /ide-final already contains this part.
  • Character: the agent floats above the app as a 3D character. The agent sets the mood of this character itself (set_mood), and an optional babble voice is available.
  • Mind panel: this panel shows the workers of the agent as brain cells17.
  • Onboarding: a tutorial with a single-player tower-defense coworld, Minion Rush.

Aaron's #28101 adds a Discovery tab and a Goal loop tab. In the Discovery tab, you can search saved findings, investigation history and recorded measurements. The Goal loop tab has an objective, verification, constraints and a duration of 1 to 168 hours, with pause, resume and end. The PR says that it is "Inspired by Mason's policy workspace exploration". It targeted /ide-mvp because goals are off on the hosted path (§3.1).

The PR opened on 10-17 and it is still open. It has two unresolved P1 review findings.

3. The primitives the UIs assume

  • Each surface has its own data model, and the models overlap only loosely.
  • The words that are most important to the profiles (goal, task, experiment, draft and workspace) have different meanings in different places.
  • Only three primitives go from end to end between a UI and the profiles: the chat turn, the native Kanban task, and the hosted XP request. /ide-final adds a fourth primitive, the layout and draft documents.
  • §3.7 puts this into a table. The table shows what each primitive asks of the profiles.

3.1 /ide-next: workspace requests, chat requests, tool calls, goals, tasks

  • /ide-next keeps its own records in the ide schema of the Observatory Postgres database.
  • IDE-owned tools wrote the goals, the continuations, the tool-call ledger and the research journey. The IDE's own MCP server gave these tools to the agent. Metta #28583 deleted that server (/hermes/mcp) on 10-21, and the hosted workspace never had a connection to it. Thus, on the hosted path, these features can only stay empty.
  • Research tasks are native Hermes Kanban tasks, not database rows. Of the features in this section, they are the only one that the hosted agent fills.

This list gives the records in sequence, from the screen of the user inward:

  • Workspace request. This is not a request for a container, a goal or a message. It is the saved UI document for one /ide-next workspace screen, and it is one entry in the History list. It holds the first prompt, the mode, the policy, the tabs, the notes, the app values and the saved views. It also holds a maximum of 12 child conversations in addition to the main conversation6. The name comes from its origin. The browser makes this document when the user submits the home-page composer18. The UI saves it half a second after each change. It goes into the workspace_request column of the ide.chat_sessions row for the main conversation10,19. Each workspace request gets a 12-character short link /s/<id>, and the Delete action archives it.
  • Conversation and chat request. Each conversation is a row in ide.hermes_conversations, and each row is bound to one native Hermes session. A chat request is one message (one turn) that operates in that session. It is not a request to open a chat. Each chat request row holds the message and context of the user, the exact /v1/runs body that went to Hermes, the run ID after Hermes accepts the run, and the end state20,1. Admission permits a maximum of one unfinished request for each conversation. The same transaction also reserves one daily credit. Thus, one workspace request holds more than one conversation, and each conversation holds many chat requests.
  • Tool-call ledger (ide.hermes_tool_calls). The approval states are approval_required → ready → running → completed, or denied. The rows came only from IDE-owned tools that have effects, and runHermesTool admitted each of these calls21,22. Since metta #28583, nothing in production calls the ledger. As a result, the ledger and the approval cards that read it (hermes-approvals.tsx) are empty for the hosted agent. But the tool rows that a user sees in the transcript come from a different source. The IDE reads the Hermes session history through the bridge, and it pairs each assistant tool call with its output1,23. The IDE also labels live activity from the tool.started and tool.completed run events23. These rows include the plugin tools of the orchestrator, but only for the session of that conversation.
  • Continuations: waits on hosted operations (XP, builds, submissions). A continuation wakes the chat when the operation completes24. Only IDE tools write continuations.
  • Goals: a conversation has a maximum of one goal, with an objective, a verification and a deadline. Most conversations have no goal25. In the retired IDE that Vercel hosted, the upstream Hermes GoalManager operated the goals. GoalManager calls itself "the Ralph loop for Hermes". After each turn, a separate judge model decides done, continue, wait or blocked. On continue, the loop sends the next prompt as a new user turn. The IDE started this loop from a Python script inside the Vercel sandbox26 (workers/hermes/goals.py). Goals are off on /ide-next, and this is intentional. Aaron's metta #27949 (10-16) says "Persistent goals target retained IDE Hermes; EC2 keeps its existing tools and scheduler"27. The hosted worker has no goal configuration and no judge configuration.
  • Research journey checkpoints: a findings log with a hypothesis, a finding, a next step and evidence. The research_journey IDE tool saves each checkpoint into ide.research_checkpoints28. But the tab does not read that table. The tab makes its entries again from the transcript, from research_journey calls or from a fixed list of IDE operation tools such as hosted_xp_wait29. The hosted orchestrator has neither of these sources. Thus, the tab stays at "Waiting for the first research checkpoint" (§7).
  • Research tasks: these are the same native Kanban tasks on board autoresearch that the orchestrator makes and the researchers do work on. The browser asks the /softmax/research control of the bridge for them, and it sends the ask as a request record. The bridge then reads the database of the board directly30,31. The Work board asks for scope league. Thus, the bridge returns the tasks that the orchestrator made from any /ide-next or /ide-final conversation of the user in the selected league31. Some tasks do not show. These are tasks from an /ide chat, tasks from a cron wake whose stored session is an /ide chat, and tasks from other leagues. Since 10-22, the board shows the native status directly. There is no outcome field and no "unverified" state, and done reads "Worker finished"32.

3.2 /ide-final: layout, draft, receipts

  • There are two owner-scoped documents for each league, layout and draft. Each document has a revision counter (§2.2).
  • ide.operation_receipts records each agent save. Thus, a repeat of the same request_id with the same arguments returns the first result. The same request_id with different arguments returns request_conflict.
  • Today the draft is a title and notes. In Phase 1, Rohit's plan has it "identify and edit real source" (§8).

§2.2 describes the two doors. These are the only IDE records that the hosted orchestrator can write. It writes them through ide_workspace.

3.3 The profiles: records, tasks, the coordinator, news

  • The orchestrator profile and the researcher profile use one shared vocabulary, ontology/ONTOLOGY.md.
  • Their research state is in a git repository inside the workspace. No UI reads this repository.
  • Their outputs for the user are the chat reply of the orchestrator, the tasks on the Work board, and ide_workspace edits. ide_say news gets only to /ide (§4.2).

The vocabulary has these parts:

  • Records: Topic (T-, "A research goal"), Hypothesis, Experiment, Result, Version, Claim, Hub, Evidence, Journal and Lesson.
  • Decisions: the decision for an experiment is promote, hold, refute or invalid.
  • League terms: Champion, Candidate, Promotion (kinds experiment, requested, bootstrap and accepted), XP request, credits and permit asks.
  • Tasks: "a bounded native Hermes assignment to one researcher". Since 10-22, there are no card kinds, no entity keys and no attempt counters: "Task meaning is its objective and instructions, not a kind/entity/attempt key"33. But the tools of the orchestrator still use card_* names.

Since 10-22, the orchestrator operates as follows (ide-distributions #30, metta #28679):

  • One input stream. "All user input, worker notifications and periodic wakes belong to one decision stream"34. §4.4 shows the queue.
  • The coordinator owns publication. Researchers stage builds in their task branch, and then they stop. The orchestrator uploads (upload_build), integrates (workspace_integrate) and submits34. Researchers get no access to workspace integrate, workspace publish and softmax upload.
  • Conversation-led subject (#25). "The coach's latest instructions choose the game, Coworld, league and player. UI selections, owned-player summaries and workspace defaults are adjustable hints"34. The orchestrator resolves these with discover_leagues and league_players. It loads the guide for each game with game_support. Since metta #28573, each IDE turn sends the owned players of the user and the selected league as hints1.
  • Explicit requests are first-class. "For build, smoke, upload or explicit submission requests, perform exactly the requested flow", with submit_requested_version and no experiment34. Statistical research is optional work, and it has its own budget.
  • Episode budget. This is a shared ceiling on hosted episodes for each workspace. The default from metta is 200. The orchestrator can only lower it (budget_limit), and it reads the budget through status (shared/ide_research_core/budget.py).

Before 10-22, the SOUL (the SOUL.md instruction file of the orchestrator) also defined five coach chat commands: task:, cancel:, pause research, resume research and promote now. These were plain-text prefixes for a coach to type into chat. The model read them as instructions to make a task, archive tasks, pause or resume research, or submit a promotion. No UI ever sent them, and ide-distributions #30 deleted them. Now the only way to pause research is the control_write tool, which the model uses when it decides to.

ide_say posts a maximum of 20,000 characters of "background news" to the chat log of the cogent, with no session35. The SOUL still tells the model to use it: "Use the bridge's final reply for user turns; ide_say for background news with a stable event key"34. But no IDE surface reads that log. Thus, today the tool uses turns to write text that only the unlinked /ide page shows (§4.2, §6.2).

The ontology never defines goal, news, priority, practice, release, draft or workspace.

3.4 Mason's client: neurons, findings, goals, drafts, one mind

  • Mason puts measurement at the center of the UI. Neurons are measured building blocks of a policy. Goals are numeric targets on one neuron.
  • Findings, neurons, links, goals and notes are durable backend resources. All of them have the mark "provisional".
  • The client frames the chat and the workers as one mind. The prompt does not permit a description of them as a team.
  • None of this is in /ide-final yet. But #28801 adds "measured-goal operations" (§2.3).

These definitions come from Mason's gateway schema (masons-ide-explorations/packages/agent-protocol/src/generated/schema.ts). The only exception is Draft, which the app gets from league submissions (apps/web/src/policies/draft.ts):

  • Neuron: "A building block of a policy: something it does or something that decides its games, measurable (in Pudge Wars: hooks landed, win rate…)". It holds readings for each version, with a sample size and a spread.
  • NeuronLink: one neuron increases or decreases a different neuron, with a confidence level.
  • Finding: something learned about the game, the coworld, the field or the policy, with evidence. Findings with the mark edge sort first.
  • Researcher: a sticky worker thread for each policy. It keeps its own history.
  • Goal: a numeric target on one neuron. After each round, the gateway (not the model) examines the latest measurement. The gateway starts another round until the goal is met, is judged impossible, or stalls.
  • Representation: a chart of what is behind the number of a neuron.
  • Note: direction from the user or the agent. A note does not have to include evidence.
  • Draft: the policy is what was submitted to a league. Each upload after that submission is a "test build".

"Chat" has three meanings in Mason's repository. First, it is the rule-based remark bubble of the agent, and this is the definition in the design doc itself36. Second, it is a chat thread, as opposed to a worker thread. Third, it is a small inline chat on a page. The workers are "more of your own mind", never "assistants, helpers, or a team"37.

3.5 Coach rules and permits

  • A permit is the request of the platform for the approval of the user before some acts, for example a league submission or a large use of credits. It is the only coach-side control that gets to the profiles.
  • The standing rules of the coach (cadence, reasoning, daily credits) are in a record that the profiles never read.
  • Aaron's replay coaching is a separate product. No profile uses it.

Where these live. profile/coach, profile/soul and the asks inbox are cogent records in the Postgres database of the Observatory platform. They are not in the ide schema of the IDE. cogent_records keeps every revision, keyed by player, collection, key and revision. cogent_record_heads points at the latest revision38. Clients read and write these records through /v2/cogents/{player}/c/{collection}/{key}. Only the coach can write profile/coach. profile/coach holds cadence, reasoning, dailyCredits and askBefore.

What a permit is. A permit is a record of kind permit in the asks collection of the cogent. Its body gives the action (submit, spend, join-team, public-post or share), the exact act (ref), an optional credit amount, a reason, and later an answer and a used time. The server makes the permit inside the request that tries to do a governed act. Then the server refuses that request with 403 permit_required. The coach answers through the answer field, and only the server sets used. A "yes" covers exactly one act, and after that act the permit is used. No timer ends a permit39. The governed acts are league submissions, XP requests and public record writes. Two things decide if an act needs a permit: askBefore, and the remaining part of today's dailyCredits. If there is no profile/coach record, every governed act asks for a permit.

How the profiles meet it. The profiles meet a permit only as a refusal, and then later as an answer. A researcher that is blocked on a permit records the ask in metadata.awaiting.permit. The cron gate of the orchestrator polls the ask, and it queues a wake when the coach answers40. Promotions read the answer through the shared client, but the path of this client is wrong in production (§6.4). Neither profile reads profile/coach itself. As a result, the preferences for cadence and reasoning have no effect on the hosted agent. /ide-next and /ide-final do not show asks at all, so their users cannot answer an ask (§6.2).

Coaching. Aaron's replay coaching takes screen and voice notes over a replay, and it changes them into structured feedback for the research loop (meeting notes, 9-25). It was in the Observatory UI, and on 10-21 that UI moved behind the staff-only /admin flag. Aaron's draft metta #28151 adds a coaching SDK and a skill cw.coaching, but it does not touch the IDE package. Today, no profile uses the coaching output.

3.6 One word, many meanings

  • "Goal", "task", "experiment", "draft" and "workspace" each have more than one meaning across the surfaces.
  • A profile change for one meaning does not help with the other meanings.

"Workspace" has five meanings:

  1. The hosted container (the "workspace" of Pause and Resume).
  2. The /ide-next request workspace, with tabs, a canvas and a research journey (§3.1).
  3. The /ide-final owner-scoped layout document (§3.2).
  4. The canonical-Git work area of the researcher (shared/ide_research_core/workspace.py). Rohit's plan links to its generated orchestrator copy as the "research repository implementation".
  5. The gameWorkspace context field.

In this report, "workspace" alone means the hosted container.

4. System map: how the UI reaches the agents

  • Each user gets one hosted IDE workspace. The workspace is a container on a shared EC2 server, and gVisor (a kernel that isolates the container from the host) sandboxes it. One Hermes gateway process in the container serves several profiles. A bridge connects out from the container to the API.
  • /ide-next and /ide-final reach the agent when they write request records (c/hermes_requests) and read response records (c/hermes_responses). Live output streams back through Redis and the open connection of the bridge.
  • The bridge sends each plain chat request to the orchestrator. No part of the UI selects a profile.
  • Since 10-22, each orchestrator input waits in one first-in, first-out queue (§4.4).
  • The bridge is metta code (packages/observatory-hosted-worker/src/observatory_hosted_worker/bridge.py, approximately 2,600 lines). Rohit wrote 21 of its 28 commits. Maxwell wrote 4, James wrote 2, and Aaron wrote 1. As a result, a change to how chat, news or tasks move is a metta change. The profiles control only what they send into the bridge.

4.1 One /ide-next chat turn

  • The IDE saves each message two times: first in its own ledger, then as an Observatory request record.
  • The bridge sends the message to /p/orchestrator/v1/runs. The runtime definition sets which profile answers. The message does not select the profile.
  • The events of the run stream back live. The IDE reads the transcript again from the Hermes session.

The steps:

  1. The browser sends a POST request to /api/hermes/chat. The IDE saves a chat request in ide.hermes_chat_requests and then returns.
  2. The IDE makes the run body1. The body has these parts: the session_id of the conversation, the message of the user as input, the selected model and reasoning effort, and an instructions string. The IDE writes this string again for each turn. The string starts with "You are the user's Softmax IDE research agent". It tells the agent to identify the game, league and player from the conversation. Then it adds a JSON block with the conversation ID, the league, the players that the user owns, and the full client workspace context. That context has the chip mode, canvasInstructions, the presentation token and the saved tabs. On the hosted path, the string also adds "Use the installed coach tools…"1. Then it adds "Use the installed profile distribution to delegate independent research on this VM… Only submit a policy to a league when the human explicitly requests submission"1. This line is the one hosted line that agrees with the profiles. These instructions go on top of the SOUL of the orchestrator itself, and the profiles cannot control them.
  3. The dispatcher of the IDE writes the request as c/hermes_requests/<uuid> with path /v1/runs48. The dispatcher operates every 3 s, with up to 4 per query. After errors, it increases its interval up to 60 s49.
  4. The bridge of the IDE workspace sees the record on the change feed of the cogent (a player that agents can address). The Hermes client of the bridge has its root at http://127.0.0.1:8642/p/orchestrator/, because the IDE runtime sets bridge_profile=orchestrator50,51. Since metta #28610, only a bridge with the application ide operates on these records31.
  5. Hermes accepts the run. Then the bridge writes the receipt, with the run ID, as c/hermes_responses/<uuid>31. The IDE waits for this receipt on the change feed48.
  6. The browser streams the events of the run through GET /v2/cogents/{player}/hermes/reads. The API relays these events over Redis to a WebSocket that the bridge keeps open52. Thus the reply text and the tool rows appear live.
  7. When the page loads again, the IDE reads the transcript from /api/sessions/<id>/messages, at 50 messages per page1. The answer of the orchestrator is only the last assistant message in its session.

The Work board and "Chat with researcher" use the same request records. They go through the /softmax/research control of the bridge (list, cancel, wait, unwait, chat), and this control operates directly on board autoresearch31. "Chat with researcher" opens a separate discussion session on the assignee profile of the task. This is the only place where a researcher talks to the user.

4.2 Where background news goes

  • The answer to a chat turn is the final reply of that turn, in the session of the conversation.
  • Work that completes later gets to the user in two other ways. On /ide-next, neither way is reliable.
  • ide_say posts to the chat log of the cogent, and only /ide reads that log.
  • A completed task reports back in the session that created it. A cron wake (XP results, credits, permits) operates in the session that the orchestrator stored last. It is possible that this session is not the chat that asked.

ide_say sends to /v2/cogents/{player}/say without a session_id, and the API reads this as "the original chat"35,53. A search of metta/packages/softmax-ide for logs/chat, say and wait finds no reader. The only change-feed reader in that package watches native_research, and only to know when to get the task list again54. Thus on /ide-next and /ide-final, the IDE never shows the news.

The user does see the wake reply. card_create subscribes the session that created the task55. The coordinator patch puts each task event in the queue for that session. Thus when a task completes, the turn of the coordinator operates in the chat that created the task, and its final reply appears in that transcript. But cron wakes are different. A cron wake operates in the origin session that the orchestrator stored last. That session is the session of the last tool call that had one56,40. Thus an XP result, returned credits or an answered permit can appear in a different chat from the chat that asked. On 10-21, before the redesign, live tests saw exactly this result: the raw wake text and "Event reported and acknowledged." (§7, Figure 18).

4.3 Long-running and short-lived agents

  • The gateway, the bridge and the orchestrator live as long as the container.
  • Researcher work is short-lived: one worker process for each task, and a maximum of one for each researcher.
  • The defaults of a task come from card_create: 7,200 s runtime and a failure limit of 2. This limit lets one retry occur55.
AgentLifetimeWhat starts it
Hermes gateway (one for each workspace)Container lifetimeSupervisor starts hermes -p default gateway run57
BridgeContainer lifetimeSupervisor57
OrchestratorResident. One turn for each inbox input: a chat line, a task notification or a cron wakeThe coordinator inbox (§4.4)
Researcher workerOne process for each task. A maximum of 1 for each researcher, and 2 in totalGateway Kanban dispatcher58
"Chat with researcher"A discussion session on the assignee profileWork board button

4.4 The coordinator inbox

  • Since 10-22, each orchestrator input goes through one durable first-in, first-out queue, the coordinator inbox. A metta patch added this queue to Hermes. Only the oldest input that is not complete operates.
  • Task events come in as native notifications. The cron job does not operate a model now. It only polls external waits and puts a wake in the queue.
  • When a turn completes, the turn consumes its input. Thus there is no acknowledgement tool.

The pieces:

  • The queue. When a profile ships coordinator.json, each turn goes through a SQLite coordinator_inbox. The orchestrator ships this file: {"scope": "research"}. After a crash, the input stays pending for recovery (metta/packages/observatory-hosted-worker/patches/hermes-workspace-coordinator.patch; metta #28679).
  • Task events. Kanban notifications go into the queue one time, as kanban:<board>:<task>:<event> inputs.
  • The cron gate. The supervisor job operates every minute with no_agent: true (orchestrator/cron/jobs.json). Its script checks only external waits: XP results, returned credits and answered permits. While a promotion is in flight, the script also does a promotion poll every 10 minutes40. If a wait is resolved, the script puts a wake input in the queue for the stored origin session ("Background coordinator wake. Read current status before acting…"). At each tick, the script also starts the oldest abandoned input40.
  • The turn. The orchestrator starts with status, does its actions, and can send ide_say.

We think that two consequences follow, but no live test examined them:

  • A chat line from a user waits behind each wake or notification turn that operates. Also, two open chats no longer operate in parallel.
  • A cron wake operates in the last session that called a tool. Thus an XP, credit or permit result can go to a different chat from the chat that asked. Task results go to the chat that created the task.

4.5 Research to champion, end to end

  • One improvement goes across the two profiles, the platform and several tasks.
  • At the permit step, the production bug in §6.4 stops the loop.

5. How the Hermes profiles are installed and live

  • Production installs the profiles from ide-distributions main HEAD, and it does a check every 5 minutes. The committed lock in metta does not control it.
  • A workspace gets a new image only when its owner pauses and resumes it. Since 10-22, startup can refuse that resume. Then the workspace stays stopped until an operator does an action.
  • Metta still patches the profiles at start time in one area. This repo can ship that change itself.
  • IDE workspaces never go to sleep, because the orchestrator ships a cron job. Open metta #28685 will change that.

5.1 What is in each profile

  • The orchestrator is a coordinator with tools but no hands. It has 29 plugin tools and a cron gate. It has no terminal and no skills.
  • The researcher is a worker with hands. It has a terminal, a 22-skill library, the research command-line tool, doctrine, and a guard plugin. It stages work, but it cannot upload, integrate or publish.
  • The two profiles share the ontology and the GotA game contract, GAME.md.

The table shows the UI primitives that each part of a profile serves:

Profile partServesUnused by any IDE surface
Chat reply/ide-next and /ide-final transcripts—
ide_sayNews on /ide onlyYes
ide_task_updateIDE tasks (c/tasks)Yes. No IDE surface makes tasks for the orchestrator
ide_workspace/ide-final layout and draft—
Task tools + researcher card skillWork board—
Records, plan, control, KB, stats, budget—All of them. Nothing outside the container reads canonical git
Publication and promotion tools—No champion or release view in any location
Platform reads and discoveryChat answers about leagues, players and games—
Experiment, review and maintenance skillsTasks that the user orders in chatNo experiment or decision view

5.2 From a merge to a running profile

  • The release workflow polls ide-distributions main every 5 minutes. It makes an image when the profile trees change.
  • New workspaces get the image immediately. Existing workspaces get it on their next Pause and Resume.
  • Production overrides the model of the profiles. But since 10-21, an IDE chat turn uses the model that the user selected.

The deploy-hermes-agent workflow resolves repos/Metta-AI/ide-distributions/commits/main and builds with --update-lock60. The workflow operates only while the repo variable HERMES_WORKSPACE_UPDATE_POLICY is preserve. Today the value is preserve. Before the workflow publishes, it does these proofs: check_chat.py, which installs the profiles and operates an orchestrator tool through a real gateway. Since 10-22, check_chat.py also does a test of the coordinator inbox. The workflow also does a profile upgrade contract check and a state-layout check. Then the workflow pushes the image to ECR (the AWS container registry). It pre-pulls the image on all hosts with SSM (the AWS remote-command service). Then ArgoCD (the Kubernetes deploy tool) puts the new autoresearch image in the runtime registry. After that, a canary pauses and resumes a retained workspace and does a check of chat. The registry changes before the canary completes. Thus the canary does not block a release (metta #28240 body).

Three facts about the software that operates now:

  • No smoke-test gate. The docs/hosting.md file in this repo expects a smoke test before the lock moves forward. That gate does not exist. As a result, every merge here gets to new IDE workspaces in a few minutes.
  • The lock is off main. The committed lock pins ide-distributions 90899586f5. That commit is on the branch of PR #30, not on main (metta/devops/hermes-fleet/applications/autoresearch/ide-distributions.lock.json). Today the only difference in the profile trees is a test fixture. But the lock does not follow main. Thus manual builds and production can become different over time.
  • Release runs failed on 10-22 from 09:16 to 11:31 PDT, at the host-install and verify step. An ArgoCD job went to its retry limit. The Datadog monitor "[IDE] Hermes Release Job Failed" fired two times. A subsequent run was successful because it used again a tag that was already published. The repo does not show which profile commit each workspace operates.

Models. Production sets all autoresearch profiles to openai/gpt-6-luna61. But the distributions have the default moonshotai/kimi-k3. Since metta #28612, each /ide-next or /ide-final chat turn sends the model that the user selected. The default is Haiku 5.51. Thus the orchestrator answers chat on one model. It processes task notifications and cron wakes on a different model. The researchers stay on gpt-6-luna.

5.3 Life of a profile change

  • The type of file controls what gets to an existing workspace. SOUL, skills, plugins and cron change with the Hermes distribution update. config.yaml, .env and memories are durable, and Hermes keeps them.
  • A workspace cannot adopt a change to the set of profiles (names or count). That change must have a migration.
  • An image that adds the coordinator refuses to start when old tasks are not complete.

On the first start, the supervisor installs each profile with hermes profile install <src> --name <n> --yes. Then it sets the model, the approvals and the working directory57. On subsequent starts, a change to only the image starts hermes profile update <name> --yes57. Then each start operates prepare.py (metta/devops/hermes-fleet/applications/autoresearch/prepare.py), which does these steps:

  • Link the image assets and write the RESEARCH_* .env values, which include RESEARCH_EPISODE_LIMIT (default 200). Also configure the shared episode budget58.
  • Add workspace integrate, workspace publish and softmax upload to approvals.deny on each profile that has the researcher guard58.
  • On the orchestrator, add the memory toolset58 (metta #28448).
  • Change the supervisor cron job to the gate script, which uses no model58.
  • Apply the Kanban settings on each start: dispatch in the gateway, no automatic decomposition, one task for each researcher, the worker profiles, and no default assignee58.
  • One time only, make the board and resume supervisor. Bootstrap only if the workspace has no .git.

The coordinator adoption gate. Sometimes a workspace resumes onto an image whose orchestrator ships coordinator.json, but the saved profile does not have that file yet. In that condition, startup refuses if the board has a task that is not done or archived. The message is "Coordinator adoption is blocked by active legacy tasks. This workspace will remain stopped. An operator must restart the previous image…"62. As a result, a usual Pause and Resume by a user can leave the workspace stopped. We do not know how frequently this occurs.

The durable-state table63 gives the items that stay after a change. These items are state.db (conversations), kanban.db, the bridge state, the canonical git repositories and workspaces, the root and profile config.yaml, .env, memories and sessions. The change replaces /opt/hermes, /opt/ide-distributions/* and the profile venvs.

Before you merge a profile change, do these steps:

  1. If you changed shared/ or ontology/, operate tools/sync_shared.py and also commit the copies. Then operate the tests of each distribution (uv run pytest -q in the folder). CI now also installs the orchestrator profile into a real Hermes64.
  2. If config.yaml changes, find out if existing workspaces must have the change. If they must, the metta prepare.py must set it.
  3. Do not rename, add or remove profiles without a migration plan.
  4. Think of a new cron/jobs.json entry as a decision about hosting cost (§5.4).
  5. Merges ship in a few minutes. Thus, test risky changes in a personal workspace first. The documented loop is the retained EC2 dev loop with brokered test accounts (metta/packages/softmax-ide/docs/ec2-development.md; metta #28062).

5.4 Workspace lifecycle

  • A workspace provisions in a maximum of 12 minutes. It is "connected" while the bridge sent a report in the last 90 s. On Pause, it drains, and the drain is never forced.
  • Each user can have one IDE workspace and, separately, one Play workspace. It is possible that the two are on the same cogent. /ide-next, /ide-final and /ide share the IDE workspace.
  • Idle sleep after 15 minutes exists, but it never occurs for IDE workspaces.

These points are important for the profiles:

  • IDE workspaces never sleep. The lifecycle check counts each cron/jobs.json that has entries as scheduled work: "Future scheduled work cannot yet wake a sleeping EC2 workspace. Keep such profiles awake"65. The orchestrator still ships supervisor, now as a script that uses no model. Thus each IDE workspace holds one of two slots on its server until the owner pauses it. The open metta #28685 from Rohit will let these workspaces sleep after 15 idle minutes. Then a message, a command or a due job will wake them.
  • Pause drains and never forces. A researcher task that operates blocks the pause. In the live session, the header Pause stopped after 90 s and did not name the task. During that time, the UI went dark (M22). Metta #28550 lets Resume cancel a drain.
  • One workspace per cogent and application (metta #28599). The key for a workspace is the player and the application. Runtimes in HERMES_SEPARATE_RUNTIMES are their own application. In production, that list has only play. All other runtimes are ide, and no runtime is also ide. A user can have one workspace for each application. A second IDE start on a different player gets 409 "Only one hosted player per user is supported"66. /ide-next and /ide-final start and adopt with no runtime selector. Thus they always get the IDE workspace67.
  • Wake from /ide-next is not clear. Only coach chat lines wake a suspended workspace. Also, /ide-next refuses to send while the workspace is not connected48,51. This is an inference. It is not important while IDE workspaces never sleep.
  • A change to the researcher count changes the profile set. Thus retained workspaces must have a migration68. The runtime definition now accepts --researchers N.

5.5 Hermes patches carried by metta

  • Metta applies six patches to upstream Hermes. The orchestrator depends on two of the patches.

The patches are in metta/packages/observatory-hosted-worker/patches/:

  • Failure classes in run results.
  • A stable operation ID across LLM retries.
  • A credential refresh on each request.
  • The current task state in Kanban failure wakes.
  • A Kanban cancel that makes sure that the worker is dead before it releases the worker.
  • Since 10-22, the coordinator inbox (§4.4).

The orchestrator doctrine relies on the fourth patch34 ("Read card_show before recovering a failure"). It relies fully on the sixth patch.

6. Mismatches between the profiles and the IDE

  • The largest gap is in the structure. /ide-next uses a design that relies on IDE-owned tools over MCP: approvals, the journey, goals, continuations and research_delegate. The hosted orchestrator never had these tools, and their server does not exist after 10-21. But each hosted turn still tells the orchestrator to use them.
  • The profiles keep their research state, champion, pause and budget in locations that no UI can see.
  • Items have the numbers M1–M24, so §6.6 and §8 can refer to them. Items that we tested live on 10-21 have a Live note. The live tests occurred before the 10-22 coordination redesign, which changed some behavior (§7).

6.1 The UI asks for things the profiles don't have

  • Each hosted turn contains instructions that are incorrect for the orchestrator, and one chip (a mode button in the UI) fails completely.
  • Complete features stay empty when the UI operates with the hosted agent.
  1. M1. Stale tool instructions on every hosted turn. /ide-next adds this text: "Use the installed coach tools and their proposal/confirmation protocol. Only the human can confirm a proposal"1. Metta #28046 retired the coach tools, and the orchestrator has none of them. Each turn also contains the client's canvasInstructions, templateSetup and a presentation.requestToken. These tell the agent to use compose_workspace, create_view, present_view and research_journey10. These were IDE tools, and their server was deleted on 10-21. /ide-final sends the same text, and now this text also contradicts the real ide_workspace tool (§8.3). The next hosted line is about the delegation of research on this VM. That line is correct, and we recommend that you keep it1. Live: the orchestrator searched its tool catalog for "workspace create view presentation requestToken" and "shared workspace research journey inspect". Each search returned "no lexical matches" and the 24 tools that the orchestrator had at that time.
  2. M2. "Improve my policy" sends a recipe built on IDE tools. The instructions of the research mode name game_contract, game_workspace, container_policy_*, research_journey, research_delegate, research_status, hosted_xp_wait and others69,4. None of these tools exists for the hosted orchestrator. Live: the chip fails completely. The orchestrator stopped and replied: "I couldn't test a teamfight improvement in this session: the required GotA contract, policy-workspace, researcher-delegation, and hosted-XP tools aren't available here… Please retry in a session with the GotA research tools enabled." It made no task, and the Research journey tab stayed at "Waiting for the first research checkpoint".
  3. M3. The chips mean nothing to the profiles. The four modes get to the orchestrator only as hint text. At one time the SOUL (the instruction file of a profile) defined chat commands. But no UI sent them, and the change #30 removed them (§3.3). Appendix E records a proposal from James: the profiles define workflows, and the chips select them.
  4. M4. The Agent workflow panel uses /ide-mvp's roles. The panel labels tasks as Analyst, Researcher or Verifier, with the kinds analysis, edit or verify8. Hosted tasks have no kinds, and they go to researcher-1 and researcher-2. Live: while task #1 ran, the panel showed "No agents running". Later, the panel listed the tasks as "Subagent".
  5. M5. Research journey, goals, continuations and approvals stay empty. Only IDE tools wrote these records, and goals are off on hosted because of the design (§3.1). The profiles record findings as claims, results and journals in canonical git, and no UI reads that location.

6.2 The profiles have things the UI doesn't show

  • The research record, promotions, the research pause and the episode budget have no UI.
  • Background news and permit asks (approval requests to the coach) never get to /ide-next or /ide-final.
  • The standing rules of the coach never get to the profiles.
  1. M6. Research records. Topics, hypotheses, experiments with decisions, results with confidence intervals, claims, hubs and lessons are all in canonical git inside the container. No UI reads them.
  2. M7. Champion and promotion. The orchestrator owns promotion_submit, submit_requested_version, bootstrap_champion, accept_champion and the procedure for champion conflicts. But no IDE surface shows the champion or gives a release control. Live: the orchestrator found a champion conflict and called control_write(pause). After "Yes, accept…" it called accept_champion (promotion P-01M5FVK6T1GTB9GNRG88X9EYSH). Then it called control_write(resume), plan_write and card_create. Only the chat prose showed these actions.
  3. M8. Pause research. control_write(pause) stops new research. The UI gives two different pauses. The first is an account research pause, made for Vercel sandboxes. The second is the workspace pause (metta #28471). Neither pause gets to the control/pause.json file of the orchestrator. Live: "Check account status" returned {"paused":false,"drained":false} ("Account admission is open") while a researcher task ran.
  4. M9. Background news is invisible. ide_say puts text in the chat log of the cogent (a player that agents can address), and neither IDE surface reads that log. The wake reply goes to the chat that made the task. For a cron wake, the reply goes to the session that the orchestrator stored last (§4.2). Live: task #1 completed at 11:51 PDT. The orchestrator used ide_say to post "Role baseline update: …" into the original chat, and the /ide room showed it. The /ide-next chat that asked for the work showed the raw wake text "[kanban] Task t_8b9ac894 completed…". Then it showed the internal reply "Event reported and acknowledged.", and then the task notice of the UI.
  1. M10. Permit asks are invisible. When a submit or a spend must have the approval of the coach, the platform makes an ask (§3.5), and the agent waits. A search of metta/packages/softmax-ide for asks or permits finds no reader. Thus an /ide-next or /ide-final user cannot answer the ask that a hosted promotion or XP launch waits for. This item comes from the code. No action in the live tests had to get a permit.
  2. M11. The episode budget has no UI. Each workspace has a shared limit on hosted episodes, which is 200 by default. Only the orchestrator can decrease this limit, and only status reports it (§3.3). A user cannot see or set it.
  3. M12. Coach rules are never read. Neither profile reads profile/coach. As a result, the preferences for cadence, reasoning and dailyCredits do not get to the hosted agent. Only the permit check of the platform uses askBefore (§3.5).

6.3 Shared words, different meanings

  • Goal, experiment, draft, chat and team shape all have different meanings in the UIs and in the profiles. §3.6 shows the picture.
  1. M13. Goal, experiment and draft. Each of these words has a different meaning in each surface (Figure 6), and none of them has an ontology entry. Goals never get to the profiles, and the "experiments" of the IDE are only XP rows.
  2. M14. Chat with researcher. This control opens an owner discussion on a researcher profile. But the SOUL of that profile says "Talk to the coordinator, not users"70. Live: the control works. The researcher gave a useful status answer with ar://evidence/… references.
  3. M15. Team shape. The labels of the panel assume analysts, a researcher and a verifier. The hosted setup has a coordinator and two researchers. Mason has one mind with workers.

6.4 Bugs and drift in the profiles

  • One production bug stops promotions.
  • You can repair four smaller problems in this repo alone.
  1. M16. The permit read path is broken in production. The shared client reads {COGAMES_API_URL}/v2/cogents/{player}/c/asks/{key}71. Hosting sets COGAMES_API_URL to https://softmax.com/api57. On 2026-10-21, https://softmax.com/api/v2/cogents/... returned the 404 HTML page of the website. But /api/observatory/v2/... returned the 401 JSON of the API. Thus permit_answer returns nothing, and a promotion that waits for a permit never moves forward. The permit read of the cron gate uses the correct /observatory prefix35. Thus the wake occurs, but the promotion still cannot read the answer. At ed1ded5, this bug is still not repaired.
  2. M17. No researcher roster. The old line "Use named assignees such as researcher-1" is gone. Now the SOUL says "You coordinate N researchers"34. But no tool lists the researchers, and card_create must get an assignee56. Metta sets the worker list of the dispatcher, but it does not tell the orchestrator58. Live (before #30): three tasks in a row went to researcher-1, while researcher-2 stayed idle.
  3. M18. experiment/SKILL.md contradicts ide-distributions #23. It still prohibits the use of a performance guardrail as a primary metric72. As a result, it steers GotA researchers away from glory.
  4. M19. Metta patches the orchestrator config at start. It adds the memory toolset to api_server (metta #28448). But this repo supplies api_server: [orchestrator]73.
  5. M20. Stale ide_workspace guidance and errors. The SOUL says "If the tool returns unavailable, explain that workspace integration is not configured"34. But the change #24, as merged, cannot return that value now. An HTTP error from the IDE endpoint shows as "cogents API returned HTTP N". The cause is that the shared handler of the plugin names the cogents API56. The open change ide-distributions #32 changes the discovery of this tool.

6.5 Platform and UI problems the profiles feel

  • These are metta problems, but each problem changes what the profiles can promise.
  1. M21. The IDE hides some tasks. The Work board shows only the tasks that the orchestrator made from the IDE conversations of the user in the selected league. Tasks made in an /ide chat are not there (§3.1). Tasks made during a cron wake are also not there when the stored session is an /ide chat. The open change ide-distributions #32 records the exact originating run of each task for the bridge.
  2. M22. Pause hangs while a task runs, and the UI goes dark. Live: Pause went to "Pause pending". Then, at 100 s, it went to "Pause blocked: work or delivery has not drained after 90 seconds… Send /stop to cancel a known live chat run, or resume to reopen admission." The UI never named the blocker, which was a researcher task in progress. Also, /stop does not apply to tasks. During the drain, the chat showed "Conversation status unavailable", the Work board showed "The work board is unavailable", and the agent panel showed "Agent status unavailable". Resume restored operation in 10 s. The system kept a message that the user sent during the drain, and then delivered it. Metta #28550 lets Resume cancel a drain. But the UI still does not name the blocker.
  3. M23. An image update can leave a workspace stopped. The coordinator adoption gate does not start while unfinished old tasks exist, and it waits for an operator (§5.3). Nothing in the UI tells the user about this.
  4. M24. One queue for everything. The orchestrator does all of its turns one at a time (§4.4). Thus a user message waits behind each background turn that is in progress, and cron-wake results can go to a different chat. This is an inference, not a test result.

7. What live testing showed

  • On 2026-10-21, from 11:27 to 12:00 PDT, we used the live IDEs as James, at metta 7737474bf3.
  • The tests showed that most of §6 is correct. Each item in §6 that the tests showed to be correct has a Live note.
  • The tests occurred before the 10-22 redesign. Since then, three items changed: the coordinator inbox, the removal of the model and event_ack from the gate, and the model selection for each turn. Thus it is possible that the news path, task routing and latency now operate differently. The stale instructions (M1, M2) did not change, and they will still fail.

The evidence is in .reports-working/ide-ux-system-map-2026-10-21/notes-live-exploration.md. The request bodies are in live/, and the screenshots are in shots/x-*.png.

7.1 What worked

From the /ide-next chat, the research loop did what the profiles intended:

  • The orchestrator found that the league champion (james-botts-gota-strategy:v47) was not in its records. Thus it stopped research for a time and asked the user. After "Yes, accept…", it accepted the champion, started research again, wrote a plan and made a task (M7).
  • A typed task: line made a task in one turn. That command is now removed, but a plain request must now do the same thing.
  • The Work board showed tasks #1–#3 in their columns.
  • "Chat with researcher" answered with references to evidence (M14).
  • Resume repaired a hung Pause in less than 10 s. A message that the user sent during the Pause arrived after Resume (M22).

Not tested: permit asks (M10), idle sleep, the permit-read 404 end to end (M16), and ide_workspace from a real hosted turn.

7.2 What failed

  • "Improve my policy" failed fully (M2).
  • The orchestrator looked for IDE tools that it never had (M1).
  • Background news went only to /ide (M9, Figure 18).
  • All three tasks went to researcher-1 (M17).
  • Pause hung, and the UI went dark (M22).

Two smaller observations:

  • Most tool calls in the /ide-next transcript showed only as "Other actions · N", with "tool call" rows that had no labels. Tool search showed as "Found the next research tool".
  • /ide-mvp login gave a Cloudflare 502 at 11:40 and 11:57 PDT. After that, Softmax retired /ide-mvp (HTTP 410).

8.3 Old problems that /ide-final keeps

/ide-final uses the same /ide-next chat path and the same hosted workspace. Thus most of §6 is applicable with no change. These problems stay: hidden news (M9), hidden permit asks (M10), the roster (M17), hidden tasks (M21), and the research chip that fails (M2), if /ide-final keeps that chip. Two items change:

  • M1 now conflicts with a real tool. RequestWorkspace still sends canvasInstructions. These instructions tell the model to use compose_workspace, research_journey, create_view and present_view76,10. The SOUL tells the model to use ide_workspace for layout changes34. Thus the model gets two different instructions for the same request, and one instruction names tools that are not there.
  • M22 is partly addressed. Metta #28550 lets Resume cancel a drain, and /ide-final now has the Pause and Resume buttons. But the UI still does not name the blocker.

8.4 A critique of the delivery plan

  • What the plan gets right. The plan gives one draft to each owner. The canonical research repository is the only source of truth, and no second mutable copy is there. The plan adds no new schedulers, queues or locks until a test shows that they are necessary. These decisions agree with how the profiles operate now: task worktrees, guarded integration and receipts.
  • What it misses. Five gaps follow. Each gap is a known problem in this report. Each gap stops or decreases the speed of one phase of the plan (Figure 19).

1. Phase 0 must also remove the old canvas instructions (M1, §8.3). The proof in the plan is "a real agent changes the intended owner's UI". In our live test, the same text sent the orchestrator into tool_search loops. Make Phase 0 remove canvasInstructions, templateSetup and presentation.requestToken from the hosted context. Alternatively, replace them with one line that names ide_workspace.

2. Phase 1 has no path from the website to the source. The canonical repository is inside the gVisor container of the user, and the bridge makes only outbound connections (Figure 7). Thus the website cannot read or write source files directly. The plan tells the team to "inspect existing file access before adding an endpoint". The current paths are the request and response records and the outbound poll of the bridge. The team built the two paths for chat turns. This is the largest design question of the plan. It is possible that the draft #28801 of Rohit ("durable IDE source") answers it. We did not do an inspection of that draft.

3. Phase 2 already has an authorization boundary, and that boundary is broken. The plan asks "what counts as publication?". The profiles already gate submission on a platform permit that the coach answers (§3.5). But in production, the permit read of the promotion path gets a 404 (M16), and the IDE does not show the asks (M10). After the team repairs M16, make Phase 2 start from that permit, not from a new "publication intent".

4. The "native completion notifications" of Phase 4 can go to the incorrect location. Task results go back to the chat that made the task. But cron-wake results (XP, credits, permits) go to the session that the orchestrator stored last. Tasks that a cron wake makes are also for that session. ide_say gets only to /ide (M9, §4.2). Phase 4 must define the chat that each result is for. If Phase 4 does not, "close the browser, reconnect, and retrieve the original outcome" can pass with the incorrect text, or in the incorrect chat.

5. "One active source-editing task" needs the roster fix. No tool tells the orchestrator which researchers are available (M17). With one source-editing task for each draft, other work waits in a queue after it. This occurs unless the orchestrator gives the tasks to the researchers correctly. The serial coordinator inbox (M24) adds its own wait.

The draft also copies records that are already there. The orchestrator keeps topics (objective, metrics, guardrails), a plan, hypotheses, claims and the champion in canonical git (§3.3). Open question 2 of the plan tells the team to "preserve the research repository's domain records". Thus the direction notes of the draft must refer to the topics and the plan, and not repeat them. If not, the coach edits notes that the orchestrator does not use as its plan.

Smaller points on ide_workspace:

  • Each tool call starts a new MCP session (three POSTs). The 30-second identity cache of the server keeps the /whoami cost low. But one initialization for each process is more easy.
  • The hosted orchestrator finds tools through lexical tool_search (M1). Phase 0 does a check of "automatic tool loading". That check must include a search for words that a coach uses, for example "layout" and "notes".
  • The server sets a fixed GoTA scope13, but the orchestrator is now game-agnostic (#25). Thus a second game needs a schema change, not a configuration change.

8.5 What this means for the profiles

  • The profile fixes in §6.6 are prerequisites. M16 (permit read) stops Phase 2, and M17 (roster) decreases the speed of Phase 1.
  • ide_workspace needs a live proof. No real hosted turn edited a layout yet. That proof is the gate of Phase 0.
  • Review ide-distributions #32 before it merges. It is the profile half of the stack of Rohit. It changes ide_workspace and the task lineage (the record of the run that made each task). Every merge here goes live in a few minutes, and this merge is the same.
  • Mason's measurement primitives come through metta, not the profiles. The measured-goal operations of #28801 will need an owner on the profile side. Either the orchestrator learns them, or they stay a UI feature.

Appendix A: Glossary

  • Bridge: the metta process beside Hermes in each workspace. It relays chat and requests between the Observatory API and the local gateway. It makes only outbound connections (observatory_hosted_worker/bridge.py).
  • Canonical repository: one bare git repository for each game in the workspace. Its main is the research record33.
  • Champion conflict: the league shows a champion that the research loop did not record. Research that depends on the baseline stops until the user makes a decision34.
  • Chat request: one /ide-next message (one turn). After admission, it runs in the Hermes session of a conversation (§3.1).
  • Coach: the human owner of a cogent, in the vocabulary of the platform.
  • Cogent: a player that agents can address. Agents read and write its records under /v2/cogents/{player}.
  • Coworld: a Softmax game environment, for example Gods of the Arena or Pudge Wars, with its leagues.
  • Coordinator: the name that Rohit uses for the orchestrator since 10-22. This profile owns the plan, the tasks, publication and the user.
  • Coordinator inbox: the durable first-in, first-out queue. Every orchestrator turn goes through this queue (§4.4).
  • Draft: this word has three meanings. For Mason, it is the policy as submitted to a league. In /ide-final, it is the title and notes of the owner, and later its source (§8). The profiles have no draft. They use version records and the champion.
  • Episode budget: a ceiling for each workspace on hosted evaluation episodes. The default is 200 (§3.3).
  • GoTA: Gods of the Arena, the coworld that the IDE targets today. The IDE code writes "GoTA" and the GAME.md of the profiles writes "GotA". They are the same game.
  • gVisor: a sandbox runtime that gives each container its own kernel layer. This layer isolates the container from the host.
  • Hosted workspace: one gVisor container for each user and application on the shared EC2 fleet. It runs one Hermes gateway and a bridge.
  • KB hub: a knowledge-base page in canonical git, "A present-tense synthesis page whose every sentence cites claims"33.
  • Neuron: Mason's measured building block of a policy.
  • Permit: the request from the platform for the approval of the coach before a submit or a spend. The platform files it as an ask (§3.5).
  • Profile: one named Hermes agent: prompt, tools, skills, config and memory.
  • Runtime (application): a named set of profiles plus an image in HERMES_RUNTIMES, for example autoresearch. All runtimes outside HERMES_SEPARATE_RUNTIMES count as the ide application.
  • Task: one native Hermes Kanban assignment to one researcher, on board autoresearch. The tools of the orchestrator still call it a card.
  • Workspace: this word has five meanings, and §3.6 lists them. In this report, it means the hosted workspace, unless a section tells you differently.
  • Workspace request: the saved UI document for one /ide-next screen (§3.1).
  • XP request: an Experience Request, that is, a hosted evaluation run that you pay for in credits.

But his goal loop and his sticky researcher have no home in a profile. Owner: Mason, Rohit and James. Blocks.

  • masons-ide-explorations/docs/agent-platform-plan.md77 says "Nothing here is built yet". But phases 0 and 1 are built.

Appendix E: Notes for future work

  • James wrote these notes as a reader of this report. They describe future direction, not the current system.

Built-in workflows in the profiles (on the four chips in §2.1). The IDE wants a set of ready-made workflows beside free chat, and other IDEs will want the same. The profiles must hold these workflows. A workflow must be quick to define, in code or in a very simple structured format. It must be possible, or necessary, for coworld owners to supply ready-made responses or knowledge for a workflow. For example, a coworld can come with a guide on how to teach it, for "Learn this game". "Review the league" can be similar to a recon skill.

The prompt then adds the workflow to the request of the user: "The user probably wants this workflow. Here is their request." As a result, the IDE can have chips like these, and it is easy to add and test new chips. This connects to M2 and M3: today the chips send IDE-tool instructions that the hosted orchestrator cannot use. game_support (#25) already loads the published guide of a game. That guide is a natural home for workflow knowledge for each coworld.

Fewer record types (on §3.3). The ontology has ten record types (Topic, Hypothesis, Experiment, Result, Version, Claim, Hub, Evidence, Journal and Lesson), and these are too many. Consolidate and reduce them.

Define the missing words (on §3.3). The ontology defines none of these words: goal, news, priority, practice, release, draft or workspace. Correct this as part of the same consolidation.

Decide what the coach records are for (on §3.5). Find out what profile/coach (cadence, reasoning, credits, askBefore), profile/soul and the asks inbox must do. Then make sure that the records that we need actually operate end to end.

Coaching (on §3.5). An important item of future work is to add Aaron's replay coaching to the research loop.
